gen.title: How DNA segments are copied through heating and synthesis
gen.orderNote: Follow the order described for how the copying process works

steps.label: first heated
steps.quote: To amplify a segment of DNA using PCR, the sample is first heated so the DNA denatures, or separates into two pieces of single-stranded DNA.
steps.orderHint: Put the actions in the order they occur

steps.label: Taq polymerase
steps.quote: Next, an enzyme called "Taq polymerase" synthesizes - builds - two new strands of DNA, using the original strands as templates.
steps.orderHint: Put the actions in the order they occur

steps.label: duplication of the original DNA
steps.quote: This process results in the duplication of the original DNA, with each of the new molecules containing one old and one new strand of DNA.
steps.orderHint: Put the actions in the order they occur

steps.label: create two new copies
steps.quote: Then each of these strands can be used to create two new copies, and so on, and so on.
steps.orderHint: Put the actions in the order they occur

steps.label: repeated as many as 30 or 40 times
steps.quote: The cycle of denaturing and synthesizing new DNA is repeated as many as 30 or 40 times
steps.orderHint: Put the actions in the order they occur
